where: Every Gleam payoff — the moment a constellation relights and the town begins to celebrate (and the dawn)
mood: Belonging, not a trophy: the motif heard in the long dusk's minor, then blooming into warm major as the sky answers.
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
A minor resolving to A major
warm soft pulse-wave lead singing the hometown melody
bright celesta and bell melody sung out
gentle festive drums with soft snare
emotional swelling celebration, warm and triumphant but a touch bittersweet, lanterns relit in the night sky

sections.name: The Long Dusk
sections.text: {hushed: a single bell and soft harp state the opening of the hometown melody in A minor, wistful and remembering the long night, then a rising swell into the light}

sections.name: The Light Catches
sections.text: {the same melody blooms in radiant A major on the warm lead over swelling strings and harp arpeggios — warmth returning, the stars relit}

sections.name: Festival Swell
sections.text: {the melody again, fuller and celebratory, bells singing the counter-line, gentle festive drums joining like a town gathering under the lanterns}

sections.name: Remembering
sections.text: {contrast: a tender, bittersweet turn to F sharp minor and D major, the melody slower and lower — remembering who was lost in the dark — then lifting back to the light}

sections.name: The Light Catches Return
sections.text: {the radiant A major melody returns in full, warm and complete; the last bar leads straight back into the melody}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme
